newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes down on peso relief.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes down on peso relief.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed 40 centavos lower at 29.60 percent on Monday due to relative stability in the foreign exchange market, which traders said was in stark contrast to the speculative frenzy seen last week.
"The peso firmed up and that takes pressure off rates. Volume was still very thin, though," said a trader. "U.S. elections may be holding up trade somewhat."
The benchmark 48-hour peso had earlier closed 5.5 centavos firmer at 7.8930/7.8980 per dollar.

Traders noted that most dealing was in the term market. Secondary rates on 90-day Cetes closed at 28.70 percent, after not trading at all on Friday, while 182-day rates closed 80 basis points at 27.80 percent.
Banco de Mexico assigned 91-day and 182-day Cetes at 29.30 and 28.63 percent at last week's primary auction.
The central bank injected 3.365 billion pesos by auctioning two credits, which it assigned at 31.68 and 31.61 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed 70 basis points down at 31.40 percent.
Total credit maturities for Tuesday were estimated at 6.322 billion pesos.
